items.title: I Had the Same AI Tools as Everyone Else. Here’s why my projects shipped faster anyway.
items.pt:
How did I build and deploy 3 fully functional apps while still in college, before I even landed my first internship?

No professor ever showed me how to do anything in college. So I did it all by trial and error, and that's why I was able to create a "real" portfolio before my SDE internship even began.

items.title: Career Ladders in a Small Startup: What I'd Do Before You Hit 30 People
items.pt:
Most engineers want to keep growing. Many of them don't know how, and in a small startup, nobody has written it down for them.

That's a real problem. Without a visible path, good engineers stall, or leave for a company that has one. But the usual fix, copying a big tech company's career framework, tends to make things worse.

Here's how I approached it as a CTO, and what I learned.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.pt: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.pt: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical sign
